selection_metric: episode-equal win-indicator Brier on TRAIN out-of-fold predictions; a sampled-outcome surrogate. No public-validation data was read for any of these decisions.

retained_baseline.name: local_interactions_averaged
retained_baseline.config: lam_intercept=0.01, lam_main=4, lam_inter=1; per-machine softmax over half-lives [8,16,32,64,128,256,uniform] scored on a held-out recent block

rejected.name: payout_magnitude_block
rejected.description: Eight extra basis dims, big_l = +1 when the lag-l outcome paid 5x or 20x and -1 otherwise, so a loss and a 1x/2x win are distinguished from a large win.
rejected.motivation: The deployed basis codes win/loss only, discarding every distinction among 1x, 2x, 5x and 20x. If the simulator conditioned the next win probability on payout size, this would recover it.
rejected.verdict: rejected - worse. Payout magnitude does not predict the next win probability here; the 8 extra parameters cost more than they add.

rejected.name: neighbour_win_sign_block
rejected.description: Three extra dims, the mean win sign of the other machines in the same episode at ticks cutoff-1..cutoff-3, excluding the target machine.
rejected.motivation: The organizer data notes say earlier outcomes on neighbouring machines can help, and the shared_change condition involves machines changing together. Episodes share one cutoff, so these ticks are legal causal inputs.
rejected.verdict: rejected - a 0.1% change, indistinguishable from noise, for 3 more parameters and an episode-join at inference.

rejected.name: two_stage_temporal_pooling
rejected.description: Stage 1 fits u_long on uniform weights over all ~200 transitions; stage 2 fits the recency-weighted u with its ridge pulling toward u_long instead of toward zero.
rejected.motivation: The deployed model is variance-limited: 282 of 768 machines choose half-life 8, about 11 effective transitions for 37 parameters, median Laplace logit variance 11.21. Borrowing strength from the machine's own long history should cut that variance while keeping drift tracking.
rejected.verdict: rejected - clearly worse, and monotonically worse as shrinkage toward the long-window fit increases. The informative negative: a machine's own long-window fit is actively STALE, so the population offset is a better anchor than the machine's own older history. This is consistent with the drift evidence and with the half-life histogram.

conclusion: Three independent extensions of the basis and the pooling structure all failed on the train surrogate. The win/loss-only 37-dim basis with per-machine half-life averaging is the best supported configuration. Remaining error is dominated by estimation variance in the local fit, not by the basis omitting a representable effect.
stated_basis_limitations: no three-way or higher lag interactions
no payout magnitude in the deployed basis (tested, rejected)
no neighbour information in the deployed basis (tested, rejected)
